uncited: By aligning samples with pixels before compositing, it bridges the gap between these two extremes, leveraging the efficiency of feed-forward warping while maintaining the visibility handling of feed-backward approaches.
The family shares the core mechanism of transforming volume data via affine operations to achieve pixel alignment before compositing.
This process generally involves two main phases: warping and compositing.
**Warping (Resampling):** The volume data (or individual slices) is resampled using affine transformations.
The goal is to transform the data such that the voxel samples align with the pixel grid of the output image.
**Compositing:** Once the data is pixel-aligned, the renderer scans the depth columns of pixels to determine the final color.
The method assumes that the viewing transformation can be approximated or decomposed into affine components suitable for this warping strategy.

While the parent Shear-warp method factorizes the view into shear and warp steps, the Affine-Transformations family focuses on the general application of affine warping to achieve pixel alignment, which can be applied to slices or the whole volume depending on the specific variant.
The Affine-Transformations Method emerged in the late 1980s as a hybrid approach to volume rendering.
This work was part of the earlier Pixar research into parallel volume rendering.
